Overview

Let's get started

Andrew, thank you for coming back to me on the refresh. Praxis was one of the first brands I ever built, so being asked back to take it further means a great deal.

Before writing this I went through every page of the current site, and then through how comparable launch safety software is sold overseas. The brand still holds up. The website has fallen behind the business: space is one bullet point on the homepage, the Contact Us button leads to no enquiry form, and there is nowhere yet to introduce the software.

What follows is a modern rebuild of the whole site, with smooth animation and a natural flow through every page, plus two new pages: one for the space sector, and one that introduces the launch risk software with a simple way to request a demo from your team. Everything is priced flat, with the Black Friday rate applied, and no hidden second quote.

Inge Loock, Creative Director at Studio Loock

The Idea

Expertise you can run.

Praxis is the Greek word for theory put into practice. For ten years that has meant engineers and project managers in the room, from requirements and tenders through to in-service support. The software is the same idea in a new form: the way Praxis thinks about launch risk, turned into a tool a launch operator can run themselves. That is the story the new site tells, and it connects everything on it. The defence programs prove the discipline. The space page shows where it is going. The software is the proof, and a demo is one request away.

Every Australian launch permit needs a risk hazard analysis that follows the Australian Space Agency's Flight Safety Code. The overseas tools we reviewed are built around American rules first. An Australian firm with defence-grade engineering credentials and a tool built for the Australian method holds a position nobody else in that market can credibly claim.

Right now the site sells Praxis as a defence aviation consultancy that also mentions space. The business has moved on. The website needs to say so.

Fixed Wing · Rotary Wing · Unmanned Aerial Systems · Space · Launch Risk Software
Who You'd Be Working With

Studio Loock

Studio Loock is a creative agency built around three connected disciplines: branding, websites and SEO. I designed the Praxis brand and the current website, so this is a refresh by the person who knows why every piece is where it is, and which pieces have earned the right to stay.

You will deal with me, Inge, on strategy, design, copy and every decision, with one trusted senior developer behind the build. No account managers, no juniors. Since the original Praxis site, Studio Loock has delivered Loyal Crush end to end (brand, website and content system) and has just launched the new Watermark Constructions website, a refresh of a long-standing Queensland business very like this one (you can see it in the sitemap section). Same discipline: a clear structure, a considered look, and a handover that leaves you in control.

What Gets Built

A modern rebuild, two new pages

The brand stays. The logo, the colours and "The sky's the baseline" still work, so this is not a rebrand. What changes is how the site feels. This is a modern rebuild with smooth animation and a natural flow through every page, built so people genuinely enjoy navigating it and learning about Praxis, the team and the software.

Part one: the rebuild

A site people love to explore

  • This is the point of the rebuild: a site so good to move through that people enjoy learning about Praxis, the team behind it and what the software can do
  • Every page gets a smooth, modern flow: considered animation as content scrolls into view, refined transitions and hover states, and a layout that carries the reader naturally from one section to the next
  • Motion with purpose, never decoration. Kept light so the site stays fast, and toned down for anyone who has reduced motion turned on

Every existing page, redesigned

  • Home, Services, About, Projects, the project page template, Careers and Contact, redesigned on the existing brand with a sharper type scale, a cleaner grid and a stronger photography treatment
  • A real enquiry form, so the Contact Us button finally goes somewhere, with a simple "what is this about" choice so enquiries reach you already sorted
  • The current build faults fixed: the doubled navigation, the repeated hero text, the raw web addresses printed above project titles, and the image filenames standing in for alt text

Projects with substance

  • The project template rebuilt around what a program manager actually wants to know: the program, the capability, Praxis's role, the phase of the lifecycle, and the outcome
  • LAND 2097 Ph4, the Army Interim Commercial Helicopter and AMCAP carried across and rewritten, with room for space projects as they become shareable

A full copy rewrite, written for search

  • Every page rewritten from scratch in the voice of the line that already opens the site, "The sky's the baseline": short, certain and premium. No filler, nothing a senior engineer would wince at
  • Keyword research first, so each page is written around what program managers, primes and launch operators actually search, with one clear search job per page and meta titles and descriptions to match
  • Redirects for every old address, organisation schema, Search Console and Google Analytics connected, mobile first and fast

Part two: the Space Sector page

What it covers

  • Praxis's space services in one place: launch permit and facility licence applications, risk hazard analysis, flight safety planning, systems engineering and program management, confirmed with you so we only list what you deliver
  • Who it is for: launch operators, spaceport and launch facility operators, payload owners and high power rocket permit applicants

Why it matters for search

  • Built around what this audience actually searches: launch permits in Australia, risk hazard analysis, the Flight Safety Code. None of that has a page to land on today
  • Links straight to the software page, so a reader who arrives for help with a permit discovers the tool, and the reverse

Part three: launching the software

What the page covers

  • What the software does and the problem it solves, in plain terms: every Australian launch permit needs a risk hazard analysis, and the software helps produce it
  • Who it is for, a few real screenshots, how it sits alongside Praxis's space services, and a short FAQ answering what operators actually ask

Request a demo, or ask the team

The people buying this are launch operators, agencies and large programs, and they buy through contracts, not a shopping cart. So the page introduces the software and hands over to your team. The main button is Request a demo, and a software enquiry form at the foot of the page covers everything else: name, organisation, email, a choice between "request a demo" and "ask a question", and a message. Every enquiry lands in your inbox already labelled as software, tracked in Google Analytics. Comparable launch safety software overseas is sold the same way: no prices online, a conversation with an engineer first.

Front and centre on the homepage

  • The software is announced on the homepage, high up, as the major new development it is: a dedicated feature section with a striking product visual, one sharp line on what it does, and a direct path to the Software page and a demo
  • The homepage story runs from what Praxis does, to the team behind it, to the software they have built, so every visitor leaves knowing it exists

Woven through the whole site

  • A "New" marker on Software in the main menu and a slim launch announcement across the top of the site for the first few months
  • Links in from the Space page, Services and About wherever the software is relevant, so people discover it from wherever they land

Honest notes, so nothing is a surprise later

Every technical claim comes from you

We will write the software page so a launch operator understands it in thirty seconds, but every statement about what it calculates, which standards it follows and what it has been validated against comes from you and is checked by you. The word "compliant" goes on the page only if you can stand behind it in front of the regulator.

Export controls, before launch

Launch safety software can fall under Australia's Defence and Strategic Goods List. Before the page goes live, please confirm with your export advisor whether the software, or anything you send after a demo, is controlled. The forms are designed so you can screen who is asking before anything is sent. This is a flag, not legal advice.

Introduced on the site, sold by your team

Pricing, licensing and contracts stay out of the website and inside the conversation with your team, where they belong. That keeps the page simple to build and simple for you to keep accurate.

Rankings are not promised

We will build every page to rank as well as it can for the work you want, and protect what the current site already has. We do not guarantee rankings, and we would be careful of anyone who does. Ongoing SEO is separate and optional, priced below.

How We'll Get There

Designed before Christmas, live in January

Kickoff Wednesday 25 November, full design presented Friday 18 December, live Friday 29 January 2027. The software page is designed first, because it is the page with the most to explain and the most information to come from you.

01

Discovery & structure · 25 Nov to 4 Dec

Kickoff call, then a 60-minute software session with you and whoever knows the product best. A full list of the current site's addresses and what they rank for. Sitemap and page outlines presented Friday 4 December. Hard deadline, Friday 4 December: the software brief. Its name, what it calculates, how it is delivered and licensed, screenshots or a screen recording, any validation evidence, and your export control position.

02

Design & copy · 7 to 23 Dec

Homepage and Software page designed and presented Thursday 10 December, the remaining pages and the Space page presented Friday 18 December, with copy throughout. Two revision rounds across the fortnight. Your technical check of the Space and Software copy is due Friday 18 December. Final design sign-off Wednesday 23 December, so you go into Christmas knowing exactly what you are getting.

03

Build · 4 to 15 Jan

WordPress build, the contact and software enquiry forms, redirects, schema, analytics and Search Console. Studio Loock closes 24 December to 3 January, so the build starts fresh on Monday 4 January. You see a private staging link, not a surprise.

04

Review, QA & launch · 18 to 29 Jan

Staging review Monday 18 January, one revision round on the built site, every form tested end to end, a full check across devices, and a walkthrough of how to add a project. Live Friday 29 January 2027, clear of the Australia Day long weekend.

On timing

The software brief is the only thing on this page that can move the launch date. If it is not with us by 4 December, the rest of the site still gets designed before Christmas, and the launch moves a week for every week the brief does. A product page written without the product helps nobody.

How We Work

"We believe good work comes from rest, not burnout, so we've built boundaries into how we work, for your sake as much as ours."

Clear communication

Revisions

Terms of Agreement

1. Authorisation

Praxis Aerospace is engaging Studio Loock as an independent contractor for the website refresh, Space Sector page and Software page described above.

2. Payment

Fees are due in accordance with the pricing above. Invoices are sent at the stages in the chosen payment plan and are due within 7 days of invoice.

3. Completion of Deliverables

Both parties work together to complete deliverables on time. The software brief, technical review and access are needed by the dates in the process section. Studio Loock is not responsible for delays caused by content or access arriving late.

4. Assignment of Project

Studio Loock reserves the right to assign trusted subcontractors to this project to ensure the right fit and on-time completion.

5. Revision During Execution

Additional fees may apply if the client requests changes to the agreed scope and objectives. Extra hours outside scope are billed at $120/hour.

6. Third-Party Services

Hosting, domains, CRM, email marketing and any software subscriptions are contracted and paid for by the client in their own name, so the accounts and the work always belong to the client.

7. Copyrights, Content & Portfolio

The client guarantees that any elements supplied are owned by, or licensed to, the client, and is responsible for the accuracy and export clearance of technical content about its software. Studio Loock may display the completed website as an example of its work, excluding anything the client marks confidential.

8. Sole Agreement & Termination

This proposal is the sole agreement between Studio Loock and the client. Additional work is authorised by written change order. Either party may terminate with two weeks' written notice, with the client liable for work completed to that point.
